title: 1 Samuel Chapter 3 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 1 Samuel chapter 3 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 1 Samuel Chapter 3 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 1 Samuel Chapter 3.

questions.question: Who ministered unto the LORD before Eli?
options: Samuel
David
Moses
Aaron
questions.correctAnswer: Samuel
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 3:1 states that the child Samuel ministered unto the LORD before Eli.

questions.question: What was said about the word of the LORD in those days?
options: It was precious
It was abundant
It was ignored
It was confusing
questions.correctAnswer: It was precious
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 3:1 says the word of the LORD was precious in those days.

questions.question: What condition affected Eli's eyes at that time?
options: They began to wax dim
They were full of tears
They were healthy
They were blind from birth
questions.correctAnswer: They began to wax dim
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 3:2 describes Eli's eyes as beginning to wax dim.

questions.question: Where was Samuel when the LORD called him for the first time?
options: Laid down to sleep in the temple
In the fields
At Eli's house
Near the ark outside the temple
questions.correctAnswer: Laid down to sleep in the temple
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 3:3 states Samuel was laid down to sleep in the temple of the LORD where the ark was.

questions.question: What was Samuel’s first response when the LORD called him?
options: Here am I
Who is calling?
I do not know
Go away
questions.correctAnswer: Here am I
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 3:4 records Samuel answering, 'Here am I' when the LORD called him.

questions.question: To whom did Samuel run after hearing the call the first time?
options: Eli
God
His mother
A priest
questions.correctAnswer: Eli
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 3:5 says Samuel ran unto Eli after the LORD called him.

questions.question: What did Eli say when Samuel told him he was called?
options: I called not; lie down again
It is time to arise
The LORD has called you
Go tell your mother
questions.correctAnswer: I called not; lie down again
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 3:5 records Eli saying, 'I called not; lie down again' to Samuel.

questions.question: How many times did the LORD call Samuel before Eli understood it was the LORD?
options: Three times
Once
Twice
Four times
questions.correctAnswer: Three times
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 3:8 shows the LORD called Samuel three times before Eli perceived it was the LORD.

questions.question: What did Eli instruct Samuel to say if the LORD called him again?
options: Speak, LORD; for thy servant heareth
Who is calling?
Here am I
Go back to sleep
questions.correctAnswer: Speak, LORD; for thy servant heareth
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 3:9 records Eli instructing Samuel to say, 'Speak, LORD; for thy servant heareth.'

questions.question: True or False: Samuel knew the LORD before the LORD began to reveal His word to him.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 3:7 states Samuel did not yet know the LORD before the word was revealed to him.

questions.question: True or False: The lamp of God went out in the temple before Samuel was laid down to sleep.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 3:3 says Samuel was laid down to sleep before the lamp of God went out in the temple.

questions.question: True or False: The word of the LORD was openly revealed in those days.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 3:1 states there was no open vision in those days, indicating the word was not openly revealed.

questions.question: True or False: Samuel answered the LORD with 'Speak; for thy servant heareth' the third time he was called.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 3:10 records Samuel's response as 'Speak; for thy servant heareth' on the third call.

questions.question: In 1 Samuel 3, which action happened first?
options: Eli told Samuel to say, 'Speak, LORD; for thy servant heareth'
The LORD called Samuel for the first time
Samuel ran to Eli saying he was called
Samuel was laid down to sleep in the temple
questions.correctAnswer: Samuel was laid down to sleep in the temple
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 3:3 shows Samuel was laid down to sleep before the LORD called him or he ran to Eli.

questions.question: What was the state of the word of the LORD during Samuel's early ministry?
options: Precious and rarely revealed
Common and frequently revealed
Not precious
Rejected by all
questions.correctAnswer: Precious and rarely revealed
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 3:1 describes the word of the LORD as precious with no open vision at that time.

medium.title: 1 Samuel Chapter 3 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 1 Samuel Chapter 3 to real-life situations.

questions.question: When Samuel heard the LORD call him the third time, what did Eli realize?
options: That the LORD had called the child
That Samuel was dreaming
That Samuel was mistaken
That the temple lamp was going out
questions.correctAnswer: That the LORD had called the child
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 3:8 states that when the LORD called Samuel the third time, Eli perceived that the LORD had called the child. This shows Eli's spiritual insight and recognition of God's voice.

questions.question: What instruction did Eli give to Samuel after realizing the LORD was calling him?
options: Go, lie down; and if He calls, say, Speak, LORD; for thy servant heareth
Run to the altar and offer a sacrifice immediately
Tell no one about the vision you receive
Leave the temple and return home
questions.correctAnswer: Go, lie down; and if He calls, say, Speak, LORD; for thy servant heareth
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 3:9 records Eli's instruction to Samuel to lie down and respond with 'Speak, LORD; for thy servant heareth' if God calls again, showing obedience and readiness to hear God's word.

questions.question: How did Samuel respond when the LORD called him as instructed by Eli?
options: Speak; for thy servant heareth
Who is calling me?
I do not understand
I will pray and come back later
questions.correctAnswer: Speak; for thy servant heareth
questions.explanation: According to 1 Samuel 3:10, Samuel responded to the LORD's call with the exact words Eli had told him, showing his obedience and willingness to listen to God.

questions.question: What did the LORD say would happen in Israel that would cause everyone's ears to tingle?
options: He would do a thing in Israel that would deeply affect all who hear it
A great famine would fall upon the land
The temple would be destroyed
The Philistines would invade
questions.correctAnswer: He would do a thing in Israel that would deeply affect all who hear it
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 3:11 says the LORD would do something in Israel that would cause the ears of all who hear it to tingle, indicating a momentous and unsettling event affecting the nation.

questions.question: What will the LORD do to Eli's house according to His declaration?
options: Perform all things spoken concerning it and bring them to an end
Bless Eli's descendants forever
Make Eli's house a place of worship
Send a prophet to guide Eli's children
questions.correctAnswer: Perform all things spoken concerning it and bring them to an end
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 3:12 states that the LORD will carry out all He had spoken about Eli's house and when He begins, He will also bring it to an end, indicating a judgment upon Eli's family.

questions.question: Why did the LORD say He would judge the house of Eli forever?
options: Because Eli knew of his sons’ wrongdoing but did not restrain them
Because Eli disobeyed the LORD's commands
Because Eli refused to build a new temple
Because Eli worshipped other gods
questions.correctAnswer: Because Eli knew of his sons’ wrongdoing but did not restrain them
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 3:13 explains that the LORD would judge Eli's house forever because Eli was aware of his sons’ vile behavior yet did not restrain them, showing the importance of accountability and integrity.

questions.question: According to the LORD's oath, how will the iniquity of Eli's household be dealt with?
options: It shall not be purged with sacrifice nor offering forever
It will be forgiven after many sacrifices
It will be cleansed by the prayers of Samuel
It will be forgotten after a generation
questions.correctAnswer: It shall not be purged with sacrifice nor offering forever
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 3:14 states that the iniquity of Eli's house shall never be purged by sacrifice or offering, indicating a severe, permanent judgment due to persistent sin.

questions.question: How does 1 Samuel 3:9-10 teach about responding to God's call in our lives?
options: We should be ready to listen and respond obediently when God speaks
We should question God's intentions before responding
We should wait for a sign before answering
We should tell others immediately without listening carefully
questions.correctAnswer: We should be ready to listen and respond obediently when God speaks
questions.explanation: In 1 Samuel 3:9-10, Samuel follows Eli's advice to respond to God's call with readiness and obedience, teaching believers to be attentive and willing to hear and obey God's voice.

questions.question: What practical Christian virtue is demonstrated by Samuel's willingness to say, 'Speak; for thy servant heareth'?
options: Obedience and humility
Pride and independence
Doubt and hesitation
Rebellion and anger
questions.correctAnswer: Obedience and humility
questions.explanation: Samuel's response in 1 Samuel 3:10 shows humility and obedience, virtues essential for hearing and following God's guidance in practical Christian living.

questions.question: What does the LORD’s promise in 1 Samuel 3:12-13 teach about consequences for leadership failure?
options: Leaders will be judged for failing to restrain wrongdoing
Leadership mistakes are always forgiven without consequence
Only the people, not leaders, are held accountable
Leadership failure has no impact on a family or community
questions.correctAnswer: Leaders will be judged for failing to restrain wrongdoing
questions.explanation: Verses 12-13 reveal that Eli’s failure to restrain his sons led to judgment on his household, teaching that leaders bear responsibility and face consequences for neglecting moral leadership.

questions.question: Based on 1 Samuel 3:14, what does the LORD's oath reveal about the seriousness of unrepented sin?
options: Sin can bring consequences that are not removed by religious rituals
Sin is easily forgiven through sacrifices
Sacrifices can always cleanse any sin
Oaths do not apply to sin
questions.correctAnswer: Sin can bring consequences that are not removed by religious rituals
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 3:14 shows that some sins, like those of Eli’s house, will not be cleansed by sacrifices or offerings, highlighting the seriousness of unrepented sin in God's eyes.

questions.question: How does 1 Samuel 3:11-12 connect the LORD’s announcement with His judgment on Eli’s house?
options: The LORD announces a significant act in Israel that includes judging Eli's house
The LORD promises peace for Eli's house
The LORD calls Eli to lead Israel again
The LORD forgives Eli's house immediately
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD announces a significant act in Israel that includes judging Eli's house
questions.explanation: Verses 11-12 link the LORD’s impending action in Israel — which will cause widespread attention — directly to the judgment on Eli’s household, showing how God's plans affect both the nation and individuals.

questions.question: True or False: Samuel was afraid to tell Eli the vision he received from the LORD.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 3:15 states Samuel feared to show Eli the vision, indicating the natural human response to difficult revelations from God.

questions.question: True or False: Samuel hid part of the LORD’s message from Eli out of fear.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 3:18 says Samuel told Eli every whit and hid nothing from him, demonstrating integrity and obedience despite fear.

questions.question: True or False: 1 Samuel 3 teaches that God reveals His word to those who are willing to listen and obey.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Throughout 1 Samuel 3, Samuel’s willingness to hear and obey God’s call results in God revealing His word to him, showing the principle of God revealing Himself to obedient hearts (verses 8-10, 19-21).

hard.title: 1 Samuel Chapter 3 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 1 Samuel Chapter 3.

questions.question: What did Samuel do after he received the vision from the LORD but before he told Eli?
options: He lay until the morning and opened the doors of the house of the LORD
He immediately told Eli the vision
He ran outside to tell others
He prayed silently for guidance
questions.correctAnswer: He lay until the morning and opened the doors of the house of the LORD
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 3:15 states, 'And Samuel lay until the morning, and opened the doors of the house of the LORD. And Samuel feared to shew Eli the vision,' indicating Samuel delayed until morning before revealing the vision.

questions.question: How did Eli respond when Samuel told him the entire message from the LORD without hiding anything?
options: He accepted it, saying 'It is the LORD: let him do what seemeth him good.'
He punished Samuel for revealing the vision
He ignored the message
He questioned Samuel's honesty
questions.correctAnswer: He accepted it, saying 'It is the LORD: let him do what seemeth him good.'
questions.explanation: According to 1 Samuel 3:18, Eli accepted the message fully and said, 'It is the LORD: let him do what seemeth him good,' showing his submission to God's will.

questions.question: What was the significance of Samuel growing and the LORD being with him according to this chapter?
options: None of his words fell to the ground, showing divine authority and fulfillment
He became a king like Saul
He was ignored by the people of Israel
He stopped ministering to the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: None of his words fell to the ground, showing divine authority and fulfillment
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 3:19 explains that Samuel grew and the LORD was with him, ensuring that none of his words fell to the ground, indicating the fulfillment and divine authority of his prophecies.

questions.question: From where to where in Israel was Samuel known as a prophet of the LORD?
options: From Dan even to Beersheba
From Jerusalem to Hebron
From Tyre to Sidon
From Egypt to Babylon
questions.correctAnswer: From Dan even to Beersheba
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 3:20 states, 'And all Israel from Dan even to Beersheba knew that Samuel was established to be a prophet of the LORD,' indicating his nationwide recognition.

questions.question: Where did the LORD reveal Himself to Samuel according to the chapter?
options: In Shiloh
In Jerusalem
On Mount Sinai
In Bethlehem
questions.correctAnswer: In Shiloh
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 3:21 says, 'And the LORD appeared again in Shiloh: for the LORD revealed himself to Samuel in Shiloh by the word of the LORD,' indicating the location of the revelation.

questions.question: What did Eli urge Samuel not to do when he asked about the vision the LORD had shown him?
options: To hide anything from him
To speak loudly
To write it down
To tell the people immediately
questions.correctAnswer: To hide anything from him
questions.explanation: In 1 Samuel 3:17, Eli urges Samuel, 'I pray thee hide it not from me,' emphasizing the importance of full disclosure of the LORD's message.

questions.question: What is the meaning of the Hebrew word often translated as 'vision' in the context of 1 Samuel 3:1, referring to divine revelation?
options: Chazon, meaning a divine revelation or prophetic vision
Ruach, meaning spirit or breath
Shema, meaning to hear or obey
Torah, meaning law or instruction
questions.correctAnswer: Chazon, meaning a divine revelation or prophetic vision
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'Chazon' appears in contexts like 1 Samuel 3:1 to denote a prophetic vision or divine revelation, emphasizing the rarity of such revelations during this time.

questions.question: Which literary device is illustrated by the LORD calling Samuel three times before Eli realizes it is God calling the boy?
options: Repetition used as a device of emphasis and revelation
Chiasm emphasizing the structure of the call
Parallelism in the dialogue
Metaphor of the lamp going out
questions.correctAnswer: Repetition used as a device of emphasis and revelation
questions.explanation: The threefold calling of Samuel (1 Samuel 3:4-8) employs repetition to emphasize the importance of the call and the process of revelation before Eli perceives God's involvement.

questions.question: According to 1 Samuel 3:14, what did God swear concerning the house of Eli because of its iniquity?
options: That the iniquity of Eli's house shall not be purged with sacrifice nor offering forever
That Eli's house would be blessed abundantly
That Eli would become a great prophet
That sacrifices would be multiplied in Eli's house
questions.correctAnswer: That the iniquity of Eli's house shall not be purged with sacrifice nor offering forever
questions.explanation: The verse 1 Samuel 3:14 declares God's oath that the iniquity of Eli's house will never be purged by sacrifices or offerings, signifying a permanent judgment.

questions.question: What reason does the LORD give in this chapter for judging Eli's house forever?
options: Because his sons made themselves vile and he restrained them not
Because Eli neglected the temple duties
Because Eli worshipped other gods
Because Eli was not faithful in battle
questions.correctAnswer: Because his sons made themselves vile and he restrained them not
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 3:13 states the LORD will judge Eli's house forever due to the iniquity Eli knew about—his sons' vile behavior and his failure to restrain them.

questions.question: How does 1 Samuel 3 relate to the theme of prophetic calling found in the New Testament book of Hebrews 1:1-2?
options: Both describe God speaking through prophets to reveal His will progressively
Both describe the end of prophecy with Jesus
Both focus on priestly duties exclusively
Both emphasize sacrifices as the ultimate revelation
questions.correctAnswer: Both describe God speaking through prophets to reveal His will progressively
questions.explanation: Hebrews 1:1-2 states God spoke in times past through the prophets (like Samuel in 1 Samuel 3) before speaking through His Son, highlighting progressive revelation through prophets.

questions.question: What historical and cultural context helps explain Eli's initial confusion when Samuel said he was called?
options: The rarity of God's direct communication with individuals during that era
The widespread polytheism in Israel at the time
The common occurrence of visions in that temple
The dominance of priestly prophecy
questions.correctAnswer: The rarity of God's direct communication with individuals during that era
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 3:1 notes 'there was no open vision,' indicating that direct divine communication was rare, explaining Eli's confusion when Samuel thought he was called.

questions.question: Which other Old Testament passage foreshadows the judgment pronounced on Eli's house in 1 Samuel 3:11-14?
options: Leviticus 20:9 about the sin of the priests
Genesis 12:3 about blessings to Abraham
Exodus 20:12 about honoring parents
Psalm 23 about the Lord as shepherd
questions.correctAnswer: Leviticus 20:9 about the sin of the priests
questions.explanation: Leviticus 20:9 warns about the death penalty for priests sinning and not restraining evil, which foreshadows the judgment on Eli's house for his sons' sins and his failure to restrain them.

questions.question: True or False: Samuel was immediately aware that it was the LORD calling him when he first heard his name.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 3:7 explicitly states, 'Now Samuel did not yet know the LORD, neither was the word of the LORD yet revealed unto him,' showing his initial unawareness.

questions.question: True or False: Eli instructed Samuel to respond to the LORD by saying, 'Speak, LORD; for thy servant heareth.'
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: In 1 Samuel 3:9-10, Eli tells Samuel to say, 'Speak, LORD; for thy servant heareth,' which Samuel obediently does when called the third time.

theological.title: 1 Samuel Chapter 3 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 1 Samuel Chapter 3 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What theological doctrine is illustrated by God's judgment on Eli's house for the sins of his sons as described in 1 Samuel 3:13-14?
options: The doctrine of divine justice and judgment
The doctrine of predestination
The doctrine of universal salvation
The doctrine of human free will
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of divine justice and judgment
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 3:13-14 teaches that God judges Eli's house for the iniquity of his sons and that this judgment is irrevocable, illustrating the doctrine of divine justice where God holds individuals and families accountable for sin.

questions.question: Which attribute of God is most clearly revealed in 1 Samuel 3:11 where the LORD declares He will do a thing in Israel that makes everyone's ears tingle?
options: Omnipotence
Omniscience
Holiness
Sovereignty
questions.correctAnswer: Sovereignty
questions.explanation: In 1 Samuel 3:11 God's declaration of an upcoming event that will affect all Israel reveals His sovereign control over history and His ability to execute His will.

questions.question: How does 1 Samuel 3:1 describe the spiritual condition of Israel during Samuel’s early ministry?
options: The word of the LORD was precious and there was no open vision
The people were experiencing many prophetic visions
The temple was full of worshippers
There were many priests actively ministering
questions.correctAnswer: The word of the LORD was precious and there was no open vision
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 3:1 states that the word of the LORD was precious and that there was no open vision, indicating a time of spiritual dryness and limited divine revelation.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal insight do 1 Samuel 3:7 and 3:19 provide about God's revelation and prophetic ministry?
options: God reveals His word progressively and sustains His prophets so their words do not fail
Prophets are infallible and never make mistakes
God reveals everything at once and then stops
Prophets can choose which words to speak
questions.correctAnswer: God reveals His word progressively and sustains His prophets so their words do not fail
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 3:7 shows Samuel initially did not know the LORD or His word, while 3:19 points out the LORD was with Samuel and none of his words fell to the ground, illustrating progressive revelation and divine preservation of prophetic message.

questions.question: In 1 Samuel 3:8-10, how does Eli instruct Samuel to respond to God's call, and what does this reveal about human readiness to receive divine revelation?
options: To say, 'Speak, LORD; for thy servant heareth,' showing openness and obedience
To ignore the call and continue sleeping
To question the reality of the voice
To run away from the presence of God
questions.correctAnswer: To say, 'Speak, LORD; for thy servant heareth,' showing openness and obedience
questions.explanation: Eli tells Samuel to respond with openness and submission to God's word, demonstrating the necessary human attitude of readiness and humility for receiving divine revelation (1 Samuel 3:8-10).

questions.question: What redemptive narrative role does Samuel's prophetic calling in 1 Samuel 3:20-21 play in Israel's history?
options: It marks the restoration of prophetic leadership and God's renewed revelation in Israel
It ends the era of prophecy in Israel
It introduces a new priestly dynasty
It signals the exile of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: It marks the restoration of prophetic leadership and God's renewed revelation in Israel
questions.explanation: Verses 20-21 show that Samuel was established as a prophet and that the LORD revealed Himself again in Shiloh, indicating a renewal of God's direct communication with His people after a period of silence.

questions.question: What does 1 Samuel 3:12-14 teach about God's covenantal faithfulness despite pronouncing judgment on Eli’s house?
options: God fulfills His promises, including judgments, according to His covenant justice
God arbitrarily punishes without cause
God revokes His covenant when people sin
God ignores human sin in covenant relationships
questions.correctAnswer: God fulfills His promises, including judgments, according to His covenant justice
questions.explanation: God declares He will perform and complete judgment against Eli's house for their iniquity (3:12-14), demonstrating that His covenantal faithfulness includes righteous judgment.

questions.question: What theological truth can be synthesized from 1 Samuel 3:4-6 and 3:17-18 regarding the human response to divine revelation and prophetic disclosure?
options: It is proper to faithfully disclose God's word, even when it is difficult or fearful
Prophets should withhold difficult messages to protect others
Divine revelations are always joyful and easy to share
Human fear invalidates divine revelation
questions.correctAnswer: It is proper to faithfully disclose God's word, even when it is difficult or fearful
questions.explanation: Samuel initially fears disclosing the vision (3:4-6), but after Eli’s insistence (3:17-18), he tells him everything, teaching that faithful prophetic disclosure is required despite fear.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is demonstrated by God calling Samuel repeatedly until he responds correctly in 1 Samuel 3:4-8?
options: Patience and persistence
Wrath and judgment
Immutability
Omnipresence
questions.correctAnswer: Patience and persistence
questions.explanation: God calls Samuel three times and patiently waits for him to recognize and respond correctly, revealing God's attribute of patient persistence in calling His servants (1 Samuel 3:4-8).

questions.question: How does the description of Eli’s physical state in 1 Samuel 3:2 serve a theological narrative function regarding divine revelation?
options: His dimming eyes symbolize the fading of old priestly authority as God calls a new prophet
It shows Eli's miraculous healing
It indicates Eli's spiritual enlightenment
It represents the perfection of the priesthood
questions.correctAnswer: His dimming eyes symbolize the fading of old priestly authority as God calls a new prophet
questions.explanation: Eli's eyes beginning to wax dim (1 Samuel 3:2) metaphorically suggest the decline of his leadership as God initiates a new prophetic ministry through Samuel.

questions.question: What combined theological teaching about God's communication and human mediation emerges from 1 Samuel 3:1 and 3:21?
options: God's revelation can be absent but He sovereignly chooses to reveal Himself again through His prophets
God's word is always openly visible to all
Prophetic revelation is unnecessary in Israel’s spiritual life
God only speaks through angels
questions.correctAnswer: God's revelation can be absent but He sovereignly chooses to reveal Himself again through His prophets
questions.explanation: Verse 1 notes no open vision and the preciousness of God’s word, while verse 21 shows God appearing again, teaching that God sovereignly controls the timing and means of His revelation.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that God's judgment on Eli’s family (1 Samuel 3:12-14) is unfair collective punishment. What does this passage actually teach about divine judgment and responsibility?
options: God judges Eli's household because Eli knowingly restrained his sons' sinful behavior, demonstrating individual and familial responsibility
God punishes innocent people arbitrarily
Judgment is random and lacks moral basis
Only the sons are judged, not Eli
questions.correctAnswer: God judges Eli's household because Eli knowingly restrained his sons' sinful behavior, demonstrating individual and familial responsibility
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 3:13 states Eli is judged for not restraining his sons' sins, showing God holds leaders accountable for both personal and delegated responsibility, refuting unfair collective punishment claims.

questions.question: What does Samuel's fear to show Eli the vision in 1 Samuel 3:15 reveal about the human experience of receiving difficult divine revelation?
options: Receiving God's word can bring fear and hesitation due to its weight and consequences
Prophets never doubt or fear
Divine revelation is always comforting and easy to share
Fear invalidates the truth of the vision
questions.correctAnswer: Receiving God's word can bring fear and hesitation due to its weight and consequences
questions.explanation: Samuel’s fear in 3:15 indicates the heavy responsibility and emotional burden that can accompany receiving and transmitting God's difficult messages.

questions.question: How does 1 Samuel 3:16-18 demonstrate the ideal relationship between prophetic revelation and priestly authority?
options: The priest (Eli) submits to the prophet's faithful disclosure of God's word, acknowledging divine authority
The priest controls and edits the prophet’s message
Prophetic words are kept secret from priests
The priest rejects the prophet’s revelations
questions.correctAnswer: The priest (Eli) submits to the prophet's faithful disclosure of God's word, acknowledging divine authority
questions.explanation: Eli asks Samuel to reveal everything without hiding any words, showing respect and submission to God's prophetic word (1 Samuel 3:16-18).

questions.question: What doctrinal truth about God’s providence and the efficacy of His word is taught in 1 Samuel 3:19-20?
options: God ensures His prophetic word accomplishes His purposes and is not ineffectual
Prophetic words can fail and be ignored
God’s presence is temporary with prophets
Prophets often fabricate God’s word
questions.correctAnswer: God ensures His prophetic word accomplishes His purposes and is not ineffectual
questions.explanation: Verses 19-20 affirm that God was with Samuel and none of his words fell to the ground, teaching the doctrine of divine providence over revelation.
